act2.location_name: Oderbruch floor east of Seelow (Seelow Heights battlefield, between Seelow, Werbig and Golzow, Brandenburg)
act2.rationale: Battle of the Seelow Heights, 16-19 April 1945: Zhukov's 1st Belorussian Front (8th Guards Army, 1st Guards Tank Army) attacked west out of the Kuestrin bridgehead across the dead-flat Oderbruch polder toward the Seelow bluff, straddling Reichsstrasse 1. The terrain is exactly the brief: open field-grid farmland with villages (Werbig, Golzow, Sachsendorf), cut by the Alte Oder and the Hauptgraben drainage canals (the balka/stream analog, which stalled Soviet armor), rising 40-50 m at the Seelow scarp where 9. Armee (CI. Korps, 20. Pz.Gren.Div., Pz.Div. Muencheberg counterattacks) dug in. The chosen point sits on the Oderbruch floor at the foot of the heights on the 8th Guards Army axis. Verified in the downloaded Sentinel-2 crop: Seelow town, the scarp edge, and the open ditch-cut field grid are all clearly visible.

act3.location_name: Halbe, Brandenburg (Kessel von Halbe, breakout of 9. Armee)
act3.rationale: The single most on-theme choice possible for a game named Kessel: the Kessel von Halbe, 24 April - 1 May 1945. Busse's encircled 9. Armee (~80,000 men) broke out westward through the small town of Halbe toward Wenck's 12. Armee at Beelitz, spearheaded by the last operational Tigers of schwere SS-Panzer-Abteilung 502 and armor of Pz.Gren.Div. Kurmark, against Konev's 1st Ukrainian Front blocking lines. Halbe itself — a small town at a road/rail junction in dense pine forest — saw point-blank tank fighting in its streets and is Germany's largest WWII war cemetery today. It is THE historical last-stand tank battle before Berlin, and a literal lone-heavy-tank-leads-the-breakout scenario. Verified in the downloaded Sentinel-2 crop: Halbe at the rail line, the A13 Autobahn (the historical Soviet blocking line), surrounding forest and clearings all visible.

notes: All URLs were verified live with curl -I (HTTP 200) or fetched during this session; nothing is guessed. DEMs: both GLO-30 tiles downloaded (32 MB each) and validated with gdalinfo; each 1x1 degree tile fully contains its act's playfield (act2 needs only E014 since the field spans 14.30-14.56E; act3 only E013 at 13.60-13.80E). Imagery: full TCI COGs are ~300 MB each, so instead of full downloads I extracted full-resolution 10 m RGB GeoTIFF crops of each playfield directly from the COGs via GDAL /vsicurl (8.4 MB and 5.2 MB), and rendered PNG previews to confirm no corrupt blocks and correct scene content (Seelow + Oderbruch field grid; Halbe + A13 + pine forest). Full TCI URLs remain available for later re-cropping. Historical-map dead ends worth knowing: (1) German daily 'Lage Ost' situation maps digitized at wwiidigitalarchives.org/maps stop at January 1945 — Feb-Apr 1945 daily sheets exist only undigitized at NARA (after 21 Apr 1945 they become 'Lage Reich'); (2) pamyat-naroda.ru (Soviet TsAMO operational maps, incl. 1st Belorussian Front reporting maps at 1:100,000 covering Feb-Mar 1945 Oder bridgeheads) returns HTTP 403 from this host (geo-block) — a VPN or EU mirror would unlock true Soviet primary operational maps; (3) igrek.amzp.pl (Mapster) works over plain HTTP only (its HTTPS cert is broken) — its coordinate search (http://igrek.amzp.pl/result.php?cmd=pt&lat=..&lon=..) is the way to find more sheets, files served from maps.mapywig.org. Both Sentinel scenes are early-April = correct season match for mid-April 1945 (bare/greening fields, no summer canopy). CRS notes for the terrain pipeline: DEMs are EPSG:4326 at ~30 m; TCI crops are UTM zone 33N (EPSG:32632-family, 32633) at 10 m — reproject one to the other before draping.
